tx.t: Today I would like to outline what glaciers are, and why they matter for sea level. Glaciers cover about ten per cent of the world's land area.
Together, glaciers and ice sheets store about two thirds of the world's fresh water. A glacier forms when snow builds up for many years and is pressed into dense ice.
Since nineteen hundred, the global sea level has risen by about twenty centimetres. This rise is caused partly by melting ice and partly because warm water takes up more space.

items.title: The history of a market town

tx.t: I would like to tell you about the history of Stanbridge. The town received its market charter in eleven eighty-five, and it became known for its pottery.
In eighteen ninety, the population was about four thousand. Over the next fifty years it grew to twenty-eight thousand.
Then things changed, because a large factory opened on the edge of town. As a result, most families moved to new houses nearby.

tx.t: In this lecture I will talk about the Great Wall of China. The wall was not built at one time. Different rulers built and rebuilt sections over more than two thousand years.

The first emperor of China, Qin Shi Huang, joined earlier walls together around two hundred and twenty-one BC. Most of the wall that tourists visit today was built in the Ming dynasty, from stone and brick.

A survey in two thousand and twelve measured all its sections at more than twenty-one thousand kilometres. It is a popular story that the wall can be seen from space with the naked eye, but this is not true.

tx.t: In this talk I will explain what psychologists know about memory and how students can use it. In eighteen eighty-five, the German psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus described the forgetting curve.
He found that people forget roughly half of new material within an hour if they do not review it. In nineteen fifty-six, George Miller suggested that short-term memory holds about seven items.
Reviewing material at increasing intervals, which is called spaced repetition, helps to move it into long-term memory. Testing yourself is more effective than simply reading your notes again.
A good night of sleep after studying helps to store what you have learned.

qs.q: How much is forgotten within an hour?

By twenty ten, the number had risen to four hundred and forty pairs, which shows that careful management can work.

tx.t: Researchers at Redbridge University carried out a study in twenty twenty to find out how students prepare for exams. They followed eighty-six students over eight weeks.
On average, the students studied for six hours a day. However, only forty-seven per cent of them used any planned method.

The students who used the method of studying in short sessions with breaks remembered more of the material a week later. The researchers concluded that how you study may matter more than how long you study.

tx.t: This lecture looks at the history and the future of electric cars. Electric vehicles are older than many people think. The first ones appeared in the eighteen thirties.
Around the year nineteen hundred, more than a quarter of the cars on American roads were electric. Petrol cars then became cheaper and could travel further, so electric cars almost disappeared.

Modern electric cars use lithium-ion batteries, which store more energy for their weight. Their main advantage is that they produce no exhaust gases while driving, though making the batteries does cause pollution.
